extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, IPRA members, and PR academics
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting or evaluating a concise professional definition of public relations that captures its purpose, role, and methods in a way aligned with ethical standards and organisational practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-word concise definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The 30-word definition reads: 'Public relations is a decision-making management practice tasked with building relationships and interests between organisations and their publics based on the delivery of information through trusted and ethical communication methods.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPRA intentionally produced a short, 30-word statement — brevity is a goal for clarity. The definition is presented as a compact formulation that practitioners and others can use as a working definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR as a decision-making management practice
rubrics_metrics.description: PR is defined as 'a decision-making management practice'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames PR as strategic and managerial (not merely tactical or promotional). When evaluating PR activities or definitions, give weight to their role in decision-making and organisational management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building relationships and interests between organisations and their publics
rubrics_metrics.description: PR's purpose is 'building relationships and interests between organisations and their publics'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises relationship-building and mutual interests (not just message delivery). Good PR should be assessed on how it fosters two-way relationships and aligns organisational and public interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of information
rubrics_metrics.description: PR operates 'based on the delivery of information'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stresses information provision as a core mechanism of PR. Evaluate communications for accuracy, clarity, relevance and whether they meaningfully inform publics rather than obscure or mislead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trusted and ethical communication methods
rubrics_metrics.description: PR must be conducted 'through trusted and ethical communication methods.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central evaluative criterion: trustworthiness and ethicality of methods. IPRA links this to its code of conduct and the need to counter 'fake news.' Assess practices for transparency, honesty, and adherence to ethical standards; avoid manipulative or deceptive tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition should answer What / Why / How
rubrics_metrics.description: A useful definition should say: 'What is PR? Why do we do it? And how do we do it?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting or judging definitions, check they address these three questions succinctly. The definition should state the nature of PR, its purpose, and its methods or approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with IPRA heritage and code
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition was crafted 'conscious of our heritage based on the IPRA code' and reflects how 'IPRA members do PR and how we think the world should do PR.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate definitions and practice for consistency with established professional codes (IPRA's code). The standard encourages definitions and practice that embody the association's ethical and professional values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to revision and community feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: IPRA states: 'Is this the last word? Experience tells us otherwise... IPRA humbly offers our definition as we see it today. All feedback is welcome.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat definitions as iterative; solicit and consider practitioner and academic feedback. Good governance of professional definitions includes review, consultation, and willingness to refine over time.
